prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"An API reference table for scanning REST endpoints and quickly comparing their method, auth requirement, rate limit, and behavior.","reading":"Readers anchor on the endpoint path, then scan the short Method/Auth/Rate limit control fields, and finally read the Description for behavior. Rows must remain identifiable as units even when descriptions wrap.","groups":["Endpoint stands alone as the row identifier.","Method, Auth, and Rate limit form a compact control-metadata block; they are short categorical values read together.","Description is explanatory prose and should receive the remaining width for readable line lengths."],"keep_intact":["Endpoint paths, especially /api/v1/exports/{jobId}/download","HTTP methods such as DELETE","Auth values such as Bearer and Admin","Rate values such as 600/min","Description words and identifiers should not be split mid-token"],"may_wrap":["Description prose across several lines","The 'Rate limit' header between words if necessary","Other short headers only as a last resort"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [282, 76, 67, 89, 205] · table 720×415px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [284, 76, 67, 89, 203] · table 720×415px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"The metadata block (Method/Auth/Rate limit at 76/67/89) is exactly right: each column is at its true one-line minimum, so 'DELETE', 'Bearer', '600/min' and all five headers sit on one line with no wasted width. The endpoint column is comfortably wider than the prose column, which correctly signals that paths are the row anchor. No mid-word splits anywhere, and rows still read as units.","problems":"Two visible faults. (1) The longest path '/api/v1/exports/{jobId}/download' overruns the Endpoint column rule and bleeds toward the Method cell — the row identifier literally crosses into the control-metadata block, which is the one thing that must never happen in an API table. (2) Description at 205px (184px of text) is far too narrow for prose: it breaks into 4–5 lines of ~24 characters, which is below a comfortable reading measure and inflates rows 1, 2 and 4 to 106px. The result is a tall, airy table whose Endpoint cells (rows 1–3) are 80% empty white space while the prose beside them is crushed.","cause":"Column 1 was set to 282 = 261 (the path) + 21 (cell padding) with zero slack, ignoring the inline-code chip padding that the endpoint values are rendered with, so the longest path overflows its box by roughly the chip padding and collides with the Method rule. Column 5 absorbed the remainder (205) and is the only column asked to hold multi-word text, so it is the one that suffers."},{"design":"r1B","good":"Same correct, tight metadata block as r1A; the 2px shift (Endpoint 284, Description 203) keeps every header on one line and every value intact. Row rhythm and cell alignment are clean and consistent.","problems":"Identical failure modes to r1A, and the 2px difference is imperceptible — this is not a refinement, it is the same design. The endpoint path still crosses the divider, and Description is still a ~24-character column producing 4–5 line paragraphs inside 106px rows. The long path in row 4 also sits alone with a large empty block beneath it, exaggerating the table's height.","cause":"Same root cause: Endpoint 284 leaves only 263px of content for a path plus chip padding (overflow), and Description 203 leaves 182px of text, far under the width prose needs; the two columns are fighting over ~20px that cannot fix either problem."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"endpoint-safe","widths":[300,76,67,89,187],"change":"Give Endpoint 18px more (300 = 279px content) so the longest path plus its inline-code chip padding clears the Method rule with a few pixels to spare — fixing the collision, the single most damaging defect in both renders. Method/Auth/Rate limit stay at their proven one-line minima (76/67/89). Description takes the remainder at 187; slightly narrower than before, but the trade is worth it because a path that crosses a column rule destroys row identity, whereas one extra line of prose does not."},{"name":"desc-first","widths":[294,76,67,89,193],"change":"Take the most conservative endpoint width that still clears the chip padding (294 → 273px content, ~12px of slack over the 261px path) and hand every remaining pixel to Description (193). This is the best reading measure the table can afford while keeping all metadata columns on one line; it minimizes prose line count and therefore row height. Slight risk that the chip crowds the divider, so it is the fallback rather than the primary."},{"name":"path-max","widths":[308,76,67,89,179],"change":"A deliberately endpoint-weighted option: 308 gives the path 287px of content, so even if the code chip renders wider than expected the identifier can never touch the Method rule, and all four endpoint cells read as clean single-line chips. Description drops to 179 (158px of text) and will run to five or six lines, so this is the option to choose if the table's job is path lookup first and prose second; it trades row height for absolute integrity of the identifiers."}]}
